findings.detail: `productFinancials` runs from line 203 to line 310 — about 105 lines in a single body that does four distinct jobs: walk the ingredient pairs and classify each cost failure (216-255), decide whether the cost is knowable (257-263), read and validate Retail Price (265-279), and derive profit/margin/status plus the cost-above-retail error (281-296). `handbooks/general/code-smells.md` sets the threshold at 80 lines for a function added in the diff. It is cohesive and well-commented today, but the ingredient loop already carries five mutually-exclusive cost branches; the next cost rule (a per-unit conversion, a currency check) lands inside an already-long body where the cost-knowability invariant (`costKnown` / `known`) is maintained by hand across two scopes.
findings.summary: productFinancials is ~105 lines, over the 80-line threshold

findings.detail: The `note` is emitted only when `cost === null || (retailPrice === null && m.retailPriceCol === NOT_MAPPED)`. So when the cost IS known but Retail Price is mapped and the cell is blank / unreadable / negative, the Profit Analysis row ships with Retail Price, Profit, Margin % and Profit/Loss all blank and an empty Note — exactly the case `docs/modules/MODULE_GUIDE.md` describes the column as covering ("`Note` (why a value is blank)"). The unit test at tests/unit/compositeFinancials.test.ts:154 pins `cost: 2, retailPrice: null, profit: null` for this row but does not assert `note`, so the gap is untested as well as undocumented. The reason is reachable — it is in the Validation Errors sheet — so this is a cross-sheet lookup the user has to make, not lost information; that is why it is low and not medium.
findings.summary: Note is blank when a Retail Price problem is what blanks Profit

findings.detail: `bomSheetRows(financials)` emits one row per ingredient line across every product, with no cap. The validator already allows up to 30 ingredient pairs per row (the `pairCount > 30` check at line 597 reports but does not drop them), so a 40,000-row composite sheet can produce >1,000,000 BOM rows — at Excel's 1,048,576-row ceiling, where SheetJS writes a workbook Excel refuses to open. The build also runs synchronously at lines 866-874, after the `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))` chunking loop has finished, so the whole sheet construction is one unyielded block on the main thread. This is the same shape the analyzer tab's export already has, so it is not a regression — recording it because this PR puts that shape on the validator path, which is the one users run on their largest files.
findings.summary: Detailed BOM row count is unbounded and built outside the chunked loop
